rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent, low rectangular gym/bar mass across all views, with the same dominant datum visible in plan, elevation, and oblique. That gives it a solid gymnasium legibility and good repair integrity. The section is modestly articulated and not arbitrarily pyramidal, so the roof/section contract is satisfied enough for an early mass. However, the access-edge response is weak: the blue frontage line is answered only by proximity, not by a clearly public void, undercut, or entry seam. Likewise, the parcel is largely occupied by a single bar, so there is limited open-space figure beyond a thin perimeter offset. It is still program-fit because the visible mass can plausibly support a clear-span hall with a subordinate roof expression, but it would benefit from a more explicit threshold carved toward the verified access edge.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Long, low sports bar with a clear datum and adjacent open edge; supports the idea of a dominant hall plus secondary service line.
A stronger public-front threshold and roof articulation over a linear sports volume; useful for calibrating entry/readability.
